groups.name: Empirical scaling of generalization error
groups.dimension: which scale variables are fitted (data size, model size, compute) and whether compute allocation is modelled
groups.comparison: Hestness et al. fit error against training-set size across four domains; Rosenfeld et al. fit a joint form in model and data size; neither models training time or compute allocation

groups.name: Large Transformer language models
groups.dimension: how far model size is pushed and what is reported about the benefit of scale
groups.comparison: the Transformer architecture is the common base; GPT-2 scales it to 1.5B parameters and reports zero-shot transfer, without a rule for splitting compute between size and data

gaps.statement: Existing scaling studies relate error to data and model size but do not model training time or how a fixed compute budget should be split, and their data-model scaling estimates disagree.

contributions.text: We show that the language-modeling loss scales as a power law with model size, dataset size and training compute, with some trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude.
We find that performance depends strongly on scale and weakly on model shape, and that every 8x increase in model size needs only about a 5x increase in data to avoid an overfitting penalty.
Under a fixed compute budget, the best performance comes from training very large models and stopping well before convergence.

author_notes: Findings and limitations of hestness2017, rosenfeld2019 and radford2019 come from literature.csv (author's table), not from the original papers: confirm before submission.
